name: One fail-loud setup script
claim_class: A claim that a deliverable's manual setup steps are ready for a human to run.
proof_obligation: When a deliverable needs a human to run steps in an environment the agent cannot reach, those steps ship as one script the human runs top to bottom, never as a prose checklist. A checklist invites the wrong order, a skipped line, or a mistyped value, and setup steps get re-run often. The script automates what it can; it checks for anything needing a human or an interactive installer instead of installing it quietly, printing what to install or set; it stops at the first real error and prints what broke and what to do next; it is safe to run again; and it states what it validated on success, or prints the exact error on failure. The delivery report names the script and shows the run that validated it.
failure_mode: A prose checklist gets followed out of order, partially, or with a mistyped value nobody double-checked, and the resulting environment ends up subtly wrong in a way nobody catches until much later, because there was never a single script that could be re-run to confirm the setup was actually correct.
origin_incident: No single recorded event is documented for this rule. It generalizes a recurring pattern: manual setup instructions given as prose steps get run inconsistently, while a single script run the same way every time either works or fails loudly at the exact step that is wrong.
